policy_title: Increase domestic food production and promote healthy eating
stated: Increase domestic food production, expand local horticulture, incentivize growing diverse plant foods, offer daily free school meals and breakfast clubs for children to Year 6, and include children in growing and preparing food as part of the core curriculum.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • Increasing domestic food production and expanding local horticulture. • Incentivising growing a much greater variety of plant food types to protect sourcing and enhanced nutrition. • All children to have a daily free school meal, made from nutritious ingredients and based on local and organic or sustainable produce and free breakfast clubs for children to Year 6. • Schools to involve children in growing, preparing and cooking food, as part of the core curriculum, so that they recognise and understand how to use basic fresh produce.

bearing_set.reason: Universal free school meals and breakfast clubs to Year 6 directly reduces the food cost burden on families, a non-negligible financial benefit for households currently paying for packed lunches or morning food.

Embedding food growing and preparation in the core curriculum is a direct curriculum-scope change; additionally, evidence links nutritional adequacy (via free meals/breakfast) to attainment and the gap for disadvantaged pupils.

Expanding local horticulture and incentivising crop diversity would plausibly improve biodiversity and reduce food-miles emissions — a mechanistically specific effect on the food-system emissions and nature indicators.

Universal free school meals (a fixed benefit in kind) represent a larger share of income for lower-income families, narrowing the food-poverty gap and the income distribution — a concrete distributional mechanism.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear on this policy: direct food-cost relief (O2), environmental effects of local and diverse horticulture (O6), educational attainment and curriculum content (O7), and the progressive distributional impact of universal in-kind food provision (O14). Healthcare (O3) effects are too long-run and indirect to clear the non-negligible bar at this policy specification.
